note: Lesson = review of ببسط/بنبسط then the new pair بزعج/بنزعج (drill-heavy, Medi's Arabic mostly in Latin letters until ~37:00, Arabic script after). D2 and D9 are the same moment (10:10-10:17, C9); kept once as D2. D1's real substance is not خلّى but انبسط written for بسط at 09:55-10:04 (B12) - merger: make sure that row is in the agreed set, otherwise add it. Two let-pass/fixed slips I could not see in the disputes and cannot tell from the agreed set (NOT added, please check): (a) 49:06 'matanzajini' (ما تنزعجيني) for 'don't get annoyed by me' - Amal said 'No' at 49:21 and modelled ما تنزعجي مني (verb takes من, not an object suffix; D2/D4); (b) 10:38 'nafs?' offered for 'everyone' when she asked 'what's everyone?' - she gave الكل (vocab-A tier 1 or tier 0 asked). D13/D14 are the same slip on the masculine then the feminine negative command 30 s apart; kept as two rows because she corrected each separately - fold if the merger treats immediate repeats as one.

rulings.why: Not an error. He asked 'Is this khalee?' (offering خلّى + happy for 'made everyone happy') and she answered 'It could be خلي but we don't want it خلي' - i.e. خلّى is acceptable Arabic, just not the drill verb. The slip she was actually flagging (09:37 'It's not happy', 09:55 'You put انبسط') is انبسط for بسط = B12, which is a different row (09:55/10:04), not this one.

row.medi_said: el takheem basat kul hadha oo ams.
row.amal_said: حم. بسط وحمس. Let's put the verbs together.
row.why: For 'camping made everyone happy and excited' he split the two verbs around the object (basat kul hada oo [h]ammas, second verb left dangling); she recast بسط وحمّس and said 'Let's put the verbs together' [10:30], then supplied الكل for everyone [10:40]. 'ams' is the transcriber's garble of حمّس.
row.english: Camping made everyone happy and excited.

rulings.why: Both readers saw this; the matcher missed it because r1 used 10:10 and r2 10:17 (his line is split across two transcript lines). Kept once here; D9 is dropped as the duplicate.

row.medi_said: so I, I think I remembered mazuj as annoying and moza- mozaj as annoyed.
row.amal_said: بالعكس. If it has this oo sound. مزعوج، موجوع، محروج، مجروح. All of them is annoyed. Feeling the thing, not causing it.
row.wrong: mazuj as annoying and moza- mozaj as annoyed
row.right: مزعوج = annoyed (feeling it), مزعج = annoying (causing it)
row.why: Asked 'which is which?' [22:54] he swapped the two participles; she said بالعكس and then named the pattern rule (oo pattern مفعول = feeling it, short pattern = causing it, later 'same pattern as مزعج: متعب' [24:05]). Filed as grammar B15 rather than vocab tier 1 because her fix is the participle pattern, exactly as بسط/انبسط is B12 not vocab; sheet rows 46-47 (annoyed | Maz3ooj | مزعوج; annoying | Muz3ej | مزعج) show both words are hers.
row.english: I remembered maz'ooj as annoying and muz'ej as annoyed (wrong way round).

rulings.why: Same slip in both readers; only the label differed. The transcript supports grammar B15: she corrected with the pattern rule, not by supplying a different lexical item.

Not an error - drill sequencing. Running the مضارع table he said 'ana baz'aj, inti,' and she said 'إنت' (do the masculine next); he then gave both 'inta baz'aj, bitz'aj' [33:05] and 'inti bitz'aji' [33:12] correctly. No wrong form was produced, and Latin inti/inta in this transcript is unreliable.

row.medi_said: ليش، ليش فرق من-- ليش فرق من WhatsApp? ... ليش فرق؟
row.why: 'Why is it different from WhatsApp' wants the adjective مختلف (sheet row 235: different (from) | mu5talef | مختلف) or غير; فرق is the noun 'difference' - a different lexical item, so tier 1 not tier 2 (tier 2 would be a wrong form of the same word). She only said كيف؟ [46:05], he repeated in English and she answered without fixing it. Best reading, B. (Secondary: من where مختلف takes عن.)
row.english: Why is it different from WhatsApp?

rulings.why: Both readers agree it is a let-pass vocab error; tier 1 fits because فرق and مختلف are different words, not two forms of one word.

row.medi_said: Don't be annoyed. Don't get annoyed by me. So this is without the N.
row.right: with the N: ما تنزعجي (مني) - the get-annoyed verb انزعج
row.why: For 'don't get annoyed by me' he picked the make-verb stem (زعج, 'without the N') instead of the get-verb انزعج; she prompted ليش؟ twice [48:57, 49:00] until he said 'you're right, it does have an N' [49:06]. Stated in English but it is a make-X vs get-X choice in the Arabic he was about to build.

rulings.why: Real: she withheld the answer and prompted until he fixed the stem choice; not a self-fix since the ليش came first.

row.medi_said: إيه بتنزع، بتنزعج لما I make retired.
row.why: Arabic-led sentence (هي بتنزعج لما ...) with the last verb phrase dropped in English though the verb is on her sheet (row 821: i tire / make people tired | Ana bata33eb | بتعِّب); after a 30 s stall she prompted 'Her.' and he produced أتعب ... أتعبها [58:22], which she confirmed. The English piece stands for one Arabic word, so not the 'whole clause is English' exclusion. r2's أتعبك -> أتعبها at 58:22 is his own fix inside the same turn before any help, so it is not a separate row.
row.english: She gets annoyed when I make her tired.

rulings.why: The two readers wrote two different pieces of one moment; the transcript supports the English drop-in (r1) as the error she prompted on, while the -ك/-ها slip was self-repaired in the same breath (S: self-fix before help).

Cannot be verified / at most S4. His 'saweroo' [08:56] and the accepted 'Sawroo' [09:01] differ only by a vowel (shadda/vowel length = F2/F3, pronunciation); her interjection is garbled as 'سعود' twice so the fix itself is not readable, and she then said 'Great'. No grammar error can be shown.
Duplicate of D2 (same moment 10:10-10:17, same wrong piece 'basat kul hadha oo ams', same bucket C9); kept once as D2.

Self-fix. He said 'Inti maz'ooj min ishi?' [25:12]; her echo 'إنت مزعوج من إشي؟' [25:24] is a masculine confirmation, not a correction; he himself said 'Oh, it'd be maz'ooja, right?' [25:27] before she said anything about gender, and she only confirmed إنتي مزعوجة. Also Latin inti/inta is unreliable here. r2 itself called it 'mostly his own fix'.

Not an error. 'Feeya za'ajatek' (هي زعجتك) is correct; she had just said both زعج and أزعج are valid and 'you should learn both' [28:13-28:56]. The recast أزعجتك [29:32] only steered him to the a- form the drill asked for ('with an a' [29:01]); she framed it as 'easier to say', not as wrong.

row.medi_said: So, hadha al-jaw, annoys me. Baz- baz'ajni. Ana biyaz...
row.why: Subject is 'this weather' (3rd m.) but he put the 1st-person prefix ba- (baz'ajni = I annoy me); she said 'almost' and modelled بيزعجني [35:09, 35:17], he repeated biz'ajni. He had started to repair ('biz-' [35:08]) but the fix was completed with her model, so not a clean self-fix.

rulings.why: Real subject-agreement slip with a voiced recast; medium because his own repair overlapped hers.

row.medi_said: So, don't annoy me. Ma ta'az-- Ma ta-- Ma ta'az'ajni. Ma ta'az'aj.
row.amal_said: Which goes first؟ الـ ز أو الـ ع؟ ... ممتاز. ما تزعجني.
row.why: He built the negative command on the past stem أزعج (ma ta-'az'aj, an extra a-/ع syllable before ز) instead of the bare you-form تزعج; she prompted 'which goes first, ز or ع?' until he reached 'ma tiz'ajni' [36:22] and she confirmed ما تزعجني [36:30]. The ز/ع ordering itself borders on S4, but the extra syllable is a stem-formation error.

rulings.why: Only r2 wrote it; transcript shows a genuine prompt-then-fix on the negative command form.

row.amal_said: ما تزعجيني. ... تزعجيني. ... ✓ Yes. ما تزعجيني.
row.why: Same extra a-/ع syllable on the feminine negative command right after he had said the masculine correctly [36:22]; she recast ما تزعجيني at 36:35 and 36:44, he repeated it wrong twice [36:36, 36:42] and got it at 36:48. Low because the relapse seconds after a correct masculine form may be articulation (S4) rather than the rule; merger may fold into D13 as a repeat.
row.english: Don't annoy me (said to a woman).

rulings.why: Real correction sequence, but likely a repeat of D13 and possibly articulatory; kept low so the merger can decide.

Self-fix within the turn. Asked for the past of بنزعج he said 'هو منزعج بي... نز-نزعج؟ Or is it انزعج؟' [40:58-41:07], arriving at the right form himself as a question; she only confirmed by analogy ('Just like we did with انبسط'). No correction of a produced form.

row.amal_said: بننزعج. ... Been catching you saying the [letter inaudible in transcript] instead of the ب.
row.why: She recast بننزعج [45:20] and told him she has been catching him using another letter instead of the ب on the we-form [45:27]; he accepted ('Oh, I didn't... بننزعج' [45:36]). Real by her words, but the transcript normalises his form to بننزعج and drops the letter she named, so the slip itself cannot be quoted - kept low per brief, nothing invented.

rulings.why: Her correction is explicit in the transcript; his wrong form is not visible, so low confidence rather than drop.

row.medi_said: Oh, oh, oh, okay. تستعمل الـ-- يتستعمل الـ telephone.
row.why: Restating her 'عم بستعمل الـ telephone' back to her as 'you use the phone' he dropped the b- and the feminine -i (تستعمل); she just went on ('آه، لأنه الـ computer خربان'). Low: casual echo and 'يتستعمل' shows the transcriber struggled with the line. 'telephone' is her own word here and is not on the sheet, so no tier-3 vocab.

rulings.why: Plausible let-pass b-drop in a form the transcript actually shows; kept low for Amal's review page rather than dropped.
